function.name: transformers_pipeline
function.description: Initializes a processing pipeline for natural language tasks using pre-trained models from the Hugging Face library. Supports tasks like sentiment analysis, question answering, and text generation. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

task.description: The task to be performed, such as 'sentiment-analysis', 'question-answering', or 'text-generation'.

model.description: The model ID of a pre-trained model from Hugging Face's model hub. For example, 'bert-base-uncased' for English tasks.

framework.description: The deep learning framework to use. Can be either 'tf' for TensorFlow or 'pt' for PyTorch.

device.description: CUDA device to use for computation (e.g., 0 for the first GPU or -1 for CPU).

tokenizer.description: Optional tokenizer to use. If not specified, the default tokenizer for the selected model is used.

config.description: Optional configuration for the pipeline. If not specified, the default configuration for the selected model is used.

function.name: initialize_question_answering_pipeline
function.description: Initializes the question-answering pipeline using a specified pre-trained model, enabling the system to process and answer questions based on the data it has been trained on. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

model_name.description: The name of the pre-trained model to be used for the question-answering pipeline, such as 'vikhyatk/moondream2'.

use_gpu.description: A flag indicating whether to use GPU for computation. If set to false, CPU will be used instead.

function.name: analyze_image_with_question_pipeline
function.description: This function takes an image file and a question related to the image, and uses a machine learning pipeline to analyze the image and answer the question. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

image_path.description: The file path to the image to be analyzed.

question.description: A question in plain English related to the contents of the image.
